about: SI Agent offline answers for Jebel Ali. Written only from cases/jebel-ali.json, cases/jebel-ali.numbers.json, cases/index.json and cases/traps.json. 'used' names the number or card each answer comes from.
overview: NISAR's HH echo rose by 3 dB or more over 497.6 ha in 144 patches between 18 Jun and 16 Oct: new structures, by the radar's rule. The 28 Oct pass was left out by our interference check. Whether water became land can't be told here: sea and sand look equally dark.

qa.q: What appeared here between June and October?
qa.a: NISAR's HH echo rose by 3 dB or more over 497.6 ha, in 144 patches of 1 ha or more, between 18 Jun and 16 Oct. A big HH rise is what new walls and structures do (double bounce). The radar rule says 'new structures', not what they are or who built them.

qa.q: Why was the 28 Oct pass left out?
qa.a: On 28 Oct our box read +6.3 dB brighter in HH while the whole NISAR frame moved only +0.1 dB. That is interference, not the ground (trap 8). Our interference check, declared before the run, flagged it, so the pass is left out.
qa.used: Card: Two-date change: 18 Jun vs 28 Oct · Measured: Interference check

qa.q: Did any water turn into land?
qa.a: Radar alone can't say here. Open sea and desert sand are about equally dark in HH: −17.1 dB vs −16.9 dB on 18 Jun (trap 11). So OmniSAR reports 'not separable' instead of a water-to-land number.
qa.used: Measured: Water ↔ land · card: Two dark patches

qa.a: The badge is Moderate: radar only, with the photo check still pending. The radar quality check passed: dark and bright ground changed by similar amounts (+0.7 dB apart). But there is only 1 pass before and 1 after, so one bad date can't be outvoted yet.
qa.used: Badge · Measured: Radar quality check · Passes compared

qa.a: NISAR has imaged this coast west of Dubai about every 12 days since 18 June 2026, through cloud, dust and darkness. The question: what appeared here between June and October 2026? Radar can answer part of that, and it tries to fool you at least five times on the way.

qa.q: Why is 16 Oct used if it was flagged?
qa.a: 16 Oct is flagged in HV only: the box read −10.3 dB vs −0.8 dB for the whole frame. The change rule uses HH, where the box moved −0.9 dB vs the frame's −0.2 dB, so the pass is used. Treat this result with care.

qa.q: Why not just compare the first and last image?
qa.a: One bad date is enough to fool you (trap 8). Comparing 18 Jun with 28 Oct would turn the +6.3 dB interference patch into a giant fake change. The plan is the median of three passes per side; with only 1 before and 1 after, that median card is still pending.
qa.used: Card: Two-date change · card: Median change (pending)

qa.a: NISAR's record here starts on 18 Jun 2026: NASA's catalogue lists no earlier pass over this box. Empty weeks mean 'not imaged', not 'nothing there' (trap 6). Anything earlier would need another satellite, clearly labelled.
qa.used: Card: No NISAR images before 18 June · trap 6

qa.q: Can I zoom in to see individual buildings?
qa.a: Not on NISAR map tiles. One zoom-10 tile address, requested 5 times on 14 Nov 2026, came back as 5 different images (trap 2). Our numbers come from the science files; sharper views must use other sources, clearly labelled.
qa.used: Card: NISAR map tile at zoom 10 · trap 2

qa.q: What do the satellite photos show?
qa.a: NASA HLS photos of the box from 18 Jun and 14 Oct 2026 show ground clearly changed around the port basin and the Palm. A team member is still comparing each radar hotspot with those photos, so the photo check is pending.
qa.used: Card: Satellite photos: June vs October · Independent check

qa.q: Who built this, and was it allowed?
qa.a: Radar can't see who, why or whether anything was allowed. It measures how the ground scatters microwaves. OmniSAR only says what changed, where, when, and how sure we are.
qa.used: Verdict: what the radar can't prove · limits card

qa.a: Every pass is compared with the whole NISAR frame: if our box moves far more than the frame, the pass is flagged. Here 2 of 2 later passes were flagged: 16 Oct (in HV only) and 28 Oct (HH +6.3 dB vs +0.1 dB for the frame). We use HH only and remove each date's smooth background.

The beam hits flat ground, then a wall, and comes straight back to the satellite. That makes new buildings and harbour walls very bright in HH. It is why this case looks for HH rising by 3 dB or more.
qa.used: Lesson: HH and double bounce · Measured: New structures

qa.q: Which direction does the radar look from?
qa.a: This case uses only ascending passes on track 056. NISAR also passes going south, but walls look different from each side, so mixing the two directions fakes change (trap 7).
